te.title: A clean heater that stopped heating

te.title: A slow decline over the shift

te.sit: Unit lined out. The monthly steam report shows E-101 using far less steam than last month, and nobody changed anything.

te.title: A cold snap

te.title: The bypass does not help

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 A clean heater that stopped heating (BFW Steam Heater E-101)
meta.caseTitle: A clean heater that stopped heating
meta.sit: E-101 was started three hours ago after a turnaround and everything worked fine. The boiler house now reports the feed water arriving at about 42 °C instead of 70 °C, and the boiler is burning extra fuel. The operators say nothing has been changed.

0.1.unit: E-101 is the flash-steam boiler feed water heater: P-101A pumps 100 m³/h of BFW from TK-101 at 18 °C through FV-101A (FIC-101) and the 100 tubes of E-101 to the deaerator at 70 °C (TT-101, TIC-101). Flash steam from the 200 kPa g header (PI-105 195 at the valve) passes XV-100 and FV-104 (FIC-104 in cascade from TIC-101) and condenses in the shell at 105 kPa g / 121.3 °C; the condensate leaves through Y-101 and trap ST-101 to the 30 kPa g return. V-104 is the manual air vent at the far end of the shell. Design: steam 9 935 kg/h, duty 6 040 kW.

rows.what: Boiler house: feed water arriving at about 42 °C instead of 70 °C; the boiler burning extra fuel
PI-100 shell 107.6 → 108.8 kPa g (design 105.0); PI-105 header 114.3 kPa g (design 195.0)
Alarms TIC-101 LO and PI-105 LO standing since 00:00:01; no operator action in the log 00:00–00:20

0.4.ctx: E-101 was started three hours before 00:00 after a turnaround and lined out at 70 °C (case sheet); the start-up crew closed the air vent V-104 at the end of the start-up, as the procedure says. BFW flow and inlet temperature are on their design values (100.0 m³/h, 18.1 °C). The operators say nothing has been changed.

R.1.p: Steam condenses on the outside of the tubes at the saturation temperature of the shell pressure, Ts = Tsat(PI-100), and gives up its latent heat λ; the BFW inside the tubes is heated. The duty is set by Q = U·A·LMTD, and the same Q must equal the water heat gain F·cp·(Tout − Tin) and the steam condensed × λ. TIC-101 holds TT-101 by moving the FIC-104 set point; FIC-104 moves FV-104. When the valve is wide open the duty is limited by the exchanger itself: by the area that can condense (A), by U, and by the driving force Ts − T (set by the header pressure). Gas that does not condense is swept to the far end of the shell and stays there unless it is vented; where it collects no steam reaches the tubes, so the effective A falls while the shell pressure rises toward the header.

R.2.eq: Q = U·A_eff·LMTD = F·ρ·cp·(T_out − T_in) = ṁ_s·λ      LMTD = (T_out − T_in) / ln[(T_s − T_in)/(T_s − T_out)]      T_s = T_sat(P_shell)      T_out = T_in + (T_s − T_in)·(1 − e^(−UA/F·ρ·cp))

1.3.safn: PI-100 108.8 kPa g (PSHH-100 trips at 250; PI-100 H alarm 200); TIAH-108 39.5 °C (TSHH-108 at 95) — far from every trip and moving away from the high limits
1.3.envn: No release: V-104 is closed, the trap discharges to the condensate return
1.3.eqn: Cold BFW (39.4 °C instead of 70) loads the deaerator and the boiler (Inference); E-101 itself is below every design limit
1.3.prodn: Duty 2 472 kW against 6 040: ≈ 3 568 kW made up by boiler fuel; TT-101 falling 6.8 °C/h
1.3.ttl: No trip within reach; the cost grows with time (≈ USD 103/h of fuel, assumed rate)

1.4.why: Every safety variable is far from its trip and the unit is moving away from the high limits. Stopping E-101 would send 100 m³/h of 18 °C water to the deaerator and lose the evidence. Investigate now: every hour costs fuel.

1.5.sp: A reduced, stable state that stops a problem growing while you investigate (not needed here: nothing is moving toward a trip).
1.5.tc: A consequence for people, environment or equipment arrives before the diagnosis is done unless you act now.

1.6.p: With FV-104 wide open the duty is Q = U·A_eff·LMTD: something has taken away either area that can condense, U, or driving force.

3.2.n: Energy balance closes: Q steam = 4 087 kg/h × 2 187 kJ/kg = 2 482 kW against Q water = 2 472 kW, so the meters and TT-101 are right and the steam really is low. LMTD at 00:20 = (121.9 − 18.1 − (121.9 − 39.4)) / ln(…) = 92.8 K, so UA = 2 472 / 92.8 = 26.6 kW/K — only 33 % of the clean 81.3 kW/K. The driving force is still there (Ts 121.9 °C is higher than design), so 67 % of the conductance is missing: area that does not condense, or U lost. After venting (T-2) UA = 5 735 / 71.2 = 80.6 kW/K (99 % of clean) and NTU = 0.694: with the design Ts 121.3 °C the same exchanger would give T_out = 18.0 + (121.3 − 18.0)(1 − e^−0.694) = 69.7 °C. The header at 110 kPa g holds the shell at Ts 116.7 °C and costs ≈ 2.3 °C; the rest, ≈ 28.0 °C, was blanketed area.

3.5.tree:
TOP: BFW outlet 39 °C with FV-104 wide open
 OR — More heat needed (load): FIC-101, TI-103 on design → no
 OR — Less driving force: header low (PI-105 ≈ 114 kPa g) → yes, a few °C
 OR — Steam cannot pass: FV-104 / XV-100 restricted → no (stem 100 %, PI-100 high)
 OR — Less condensing area (UA 33 % of clean)
    OR — Non-condensable gas blankets the far end
       OR — gas carried in continuously with the flash steam
       OR — start-up air left in the shell
    OR — Condensate floods the lower tubes → no (bottom hot, trap normal)
 OR — Lower U: scale, oil film → no (ΔP normal; venting restores)
 OR — TT-101 reads low → no (TIAH-108, TG-101 agree)
3.5.cut: Two single-element cut sets act at the same time: {gas in the shell with V-104 shut} takes ≈ 28 °C and {header 110 instead of 195 kPa g} takes ≈ 2.3 °C. Neither alone explains 39 °C; the gas dominates.

rows.st: “FV-104 is wide open — the steam valve must be too small.”
rows.how: Not true: the same valve at 100 % passed 10 130 kg/h (more than the 9 935 design) as soon as the shell was vented (T-2)
No set point, mode or valve change in the event log; V-104 was shut at the end of the start-up as the procedure says — a normal step that let the gas stay

3.8.n: The only change that lines up is the end of the start-up: V-104 was shut and the shell had no way out for gas. Whether the gas was a one-off (start-up air) or keeps arriving with the steam decides the fix — T-3 tells them apart.

3.10.n: Agreed: with FV-104 wide open the exchanger sets the duty; gas at the far end takes area away and raises the shell pressure.

3.11.n: The statement names only the symptom

5.1.proof: Ev-9 far end of the shell cool at the top, vent line cool; Ev-10 UA 33 % of clean; T-2: gas-like discharge then dry steam, TT-101 38.8 → 67.4 °C in 10 min, UA back to 99 %; T-3: decline returned at −9.4 °C/h with V-104 shut
5.1.mech: The flash steam carries a little non-condensable gas → the steam flows to the tubes and condenses, the gas is swept to the top of the far end of the shell and, with V-104 shut, stays there → it blankets a growing share of the tubes (67 % of the conductance lost at 00:20) → less condensing area: the shell pressure rises toward the header (108.8 kPa g) so less steam can enter even with FV-104 wide open (4 087 kg/h) → the duty falls to 2 472 kW and TT-101 to 39.4 °C, still falling. On top, the header at ≈ 110 kPa g instead of 195 lowers Ts and costs ≈ 2.3 °C even with a clean shell (WH-2).

Rev C: automatic air vent AAV-101 with TI-102 / TAL-102 at the far end (MOC)

Ask the upstream plant for the header rate and when 195 kPa g will be back

rows.act: V-104 0 → 100 % (purge the gas that came back during T-3)
Rev C AAV-101 with TI-102 / TAL-102 put in service (MOC), V-104 15 → 0 %

rows.pval: back to ≈ 67 °C (the header-limited value seen in T-2, 67.4 °C)

5.7.n: With the 15 % crack TT-101 averaged 67.2 °C (02:00–02:40) for 112 kg/h of vent steam (1.2 % of FIC-104); with rev C and V-104 shut it averaged 67.0 °C for 92 kg/h (1.0 %), TI-102 106.6 °C against TI-100 117.5 °C (TAL-102 standing: the AAV sees gas and keeps venting). Residual: 70 °C is not reachable until the header is back — at 111 kPa g the best is ≈ 67.4 °C. TT-101 sits on the 67 °C TIC-101 LO alarm and the alarm chattered 504 times in the last hour (deadband 0.05 K).

5.8.rule: When a steam heater falls off with its valve wide open and the shell pressure climbs toward the header, feel the far end of the shell and vent it before you blame the valve or the tubes.

6.0.n: T-2 gave the predicted rise to the header-limited value and T-3 the predicted decline; the vent brought TT-101 from 58.0 to ≈ 67 °C. The outcome is limited by the header, which the team cannot fix.

rows.m: Rev C automatic air vent AAV-101 with TI-102 and TAL-102 (vent line cold = gas at the vent) at the far end of the shell
Start-up procedure: after V-104 is closed, leave it cracked 3–15 % unless rev B / rev C is in service
Blanketing alarm: PI-100 within 10 kPa of PI-105 while FV-104 > 95 % (set points assumed, to be tuned)
Header pressure: agree a minimum with the upstream plant (PI-105 LO 150 kPa g already exists)

6.1.kpi: UA = Q / LMTD of E-101 each shift (target ≥ 90 % of the clean value)

rows.i: TT-101 back from 58 to ≈ 67 °C: ≈ 1 074 kW less boiler make-up
Rev C vents only when gas is there (92 kg/h now) and alarms on TAL-102 — no operator has to remember V-104
Continuous vent steam ≈ 92–112 kg/h is a running loss (≈ USD 16–20 k a year, assumed steam value)
TIC-101 LO alarm chatters at the header-limited 67 °C (504 times in an hour): add a delay or deadband, or accept a lower target while the header is low

hz.cons: Steam lost to atmosphere, plume at the platform
hz.sg: TI-102 reads hot at the vent; vent discharge to a safe location; V-104 / isolation upstream of AAV-101
TAL-102 alarm; UA KPI each shift; V-104 as manual back-up

hz.cause: Shell below atmospheric at low load or after a trip
hz.sg: Vacuum breaker VB-101 already lets air in — vent at the next start-up

6.3.fut: A steam heater fed by flash steam needs a continuous way out for gas; a manual vent that is shut after start-up is not one.

6.4.how: A week of the 3 568 kW deficit avoided at USD 8/GJ of fuel (assumed rate) ≈ USD 103/h

6.5.again:
Look at the shell pressure against the header, not only at the valve.
Close the energy balance before blaming an instrument.
Use UA = Q / LMTD to separate area, U and driving force.
Run the cheap, reversible test first (open a vent for 10 min) and write the kill criterion before you do it.
6.5.never:
Never call a control valve undersized because it is wide open — ask what is limiting the flow behind it.
Never close the only air vent of a flash-steam heater and walk away.

hyp.cause: Condensate backing up into the shell (strainer Y-101 / trap ST-101 restriction)
hyp.cat: Steam supply & condensate (header, XV-100, FV-104, trap, return)
hyp.ifthen: If condensate backs up, the lower tubes flood: a cool band along the BOTTOM of the shell, the trap discharges in weak spurts; V-103 restores
hyp.key: Bottom of the shell cool; trap spurts
hyp.fals: Bottom hot; trap cycling normally; venting restores

hyp.ifthen: If the tubes were scaled, PDI-109 would rise and venting would change nothing
hyp.fals: PDI-109 on design; T-2 restores UA

hyp.cause: Oil film on the shell side of the tubes
hyp.ifthen: If an oil film lowered U, FV-104 and PI-100 would rise, but venting would change nothing
hyp.fals: T-2 restores UA to the clean value

hyp.cause: TT-101 reads low (the water is really hotter)
hyp.ifthen: If TT-101 read low, TIAH-108 and TG-101 would read higher and Q steam would exceed Q water
hyp.fals: TIAH-108 = TG-101 = TT-101; Q steam = Q water

hyp.cause: FV-104 / XV-100 not passing the steam the output asks for
hyp.cat: Steam supply & condensate (header, XV-100, FV-104, trap, return)
hyp.ifthen: If the valve restricted the steam, PI-100 would FALL below design and the stem would not be at 100 %
hyp.fals: PI-100 above design; stem fully open; 10 000 kg/h through the same valve once vented

hyp.cause: Higher load: more BFW or colder BFW
hyp.ifthen: If the load had risen, FIC-101 would be high or TI-103 low

tests.title: Field round of stations 7–12 (look only)
tests.move: Nothing moved: read PI-105, PG-100, TG-100, TG-101, TG-107, PG-110; feel the shell (IR gun) end to end, top and bottom; look at V-104, the vent line and trap ST-101; check the FV-104 stem.

WH-1.note: top of the far end cool, bottom hot, vent line cold

WH-2.note: PI-105 well below 195 kPa g at the valve

WH-4.note: bottom of the shell cool, trap in weak spurts

tests.kill: Bottom hot and trap normal → WH-4 killed; TG-101 within 1 °C of TT-101 → WH-7 killed; stem at 100 % with PI-100 above design → WH-8 killed; far end hot at the top → WH-1 killed.
tests.stop: None — observation only (hot surfaces: IR gun, gloves)

res.obs: Steam end ≈ 122 °C. Top of the far end ≈ 52 °C (noticeably cooler). Bottom of the shell ≈ 120 °C. V-104 closed. The vent line feels cool. Trap cycling normally: condensate with a little flash. PI-105 114.0, PG-100 109 kPa g, TG-100 121.9, TG-101 39.0, TG-107 120.0 °C, PG-110 30 kPa g; FV-104 stem fully open.

tests.title: Vent test: V-104 fully open for 10 min
tests.move: At 00:25:00 open V-104 0 → 100 % in the field; nothing else touched; watch the discharge, TT-101, FIC-104, PI-100 for 10 min.

WH-1.note: gas, then dry steam at the vent; TT-101 up by > 20 °C within 10 min, to the header-limited value (< 70)

WH-3.note: same response (start-up air also vents) — T-3 separates them

WH-6.note: an oil film does not vent

tests.kill: TT-101 rises > 5 °C in 10 min → WH-5 and WH-6 killed; rises < 1 °C → WH-1 and WH-3 killed.
tests.stop: Stop (close V-104) if PI-100 < 20 kPa g (shell heading to vacuum), TIAH-108 > 85 °C, or banging in the shell; nobody in line with the vent discharge

res.obs: Mostly non-condensable gas with some steam: a thin, cool, wispy discharge for ≈ 2 min, then dry steam blowing: hot, visible plume. TT-101 38.8 → 55.0 (+1 min) → 64.3 (+2) → 67.4 °C (+10); FIC-104 3 994 → 10 130 kg/h; PI-100 109.6 → 77.1 kPa g; far end now 116 °C; vent ≈ 718 kg/h.

tests.title: Close V-104 again and watch for 60 min
tests.move: At 00:35:00 close V-104 (100 → 0 %); nothing else touched; hold 60 min.

WH-1.note: gas keeps arriving with the steam: TT-101 falls again, PI-100 rises

WH-3.note: the start-up air is gone: TT-101 stays ≈ 67 °C

tests.kill: TT-101 falls > 3 °C in 60 min → WH-3 killed, WH-1 confirmed; stays within ±1 °C → WH-1 (continuous gas) killed.

res.obs: TT-101 67.4 → 66.3 (+10 min) → 58.0 °C (+60 min), −9.4 °C/h; PI-100 77.1 → 93.5 kPa g; FIC-104 10 130 → 7 631 kg/h; FV-104 stayed at 100 %; the far end cooled again (Steam end ≈ 120 °C. Top of the far end ≈ 62 °C (noticeably cooler). Bottom of the shell ≈ 118 °C.)
